index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents an overview of the I³-CSS framework, a speech synthesis system designed for dialogue contexts, structured into four main components: Intra-modal Interaction Modules, Inter-modal Interaction Modules, Text Encoder, and Speech Synthesizer. The global layout is divided into two main sections: the left side shows the high-level pipeline, while the right side provides detailed architectures of the interaction modules.

On the left, the top-left corner displays a 'Current Dialogue' panel illustrating a conversation history with alternating text (t₁, t₂, ..., tₙ) and speech (s₁, s₂, ..., sₙ) turns, each represented by a speaker icon, text bubble, and waveform. The target utterance (tₙ, sₙ) is marked as used only during training. From this dialogue history, historical text and speech sequences are fed into the interaction modules.

The first component, 'Intra-modal Interaction Modules', processes historical text-to-next text (HT-NT) and historical speech-to-next speech (HS-NS) interactions. These are represented by blue and pink rectangular boxes respectively, receiving inputs t₁→N−1 and s₁→N−1. Outputs Fᵗ⁻ⁱⁿᵗʳᵃ and Fˢ⁻ⁱⁿᵗʳᵃ are generated.

The second component, 'Inter-modal Interaction Modules', handles cross-modal interactions: historical text-to-next speech (HT-NS) and historical speech-to-next text (HS-NT), again shown in blue and pink boxes. Inputs include t₁→N−1, s₂→N−1, t₂→N−1, and s₁→N−1. Outputs are Fᵗ⁻ⁱⁿᵗᵉʳ and Fˢ⁻ⁱⁿᵗᵉʳ.

The third component, 'Text Encoder', processes the current target text tₙ to produce Pₙ. This module is depicted as a gray box.

All feature representations from the interaction modules and text encoder are aggregated by the 'Feature Aggregator' (a tall orange rectangle), which feeds into the 'Acoustic Decoder' (gray rectangle) and then the 'Vocoder' (yellow rectangle), producing the final synthesized speech waveform shown on the far right.

The right side of the figure details the internal structure of the interaction modules. Each module contains a 'Historical Encoder' (blue for text, pink for speech) that processes past sequences (e.g., Hᵗᵉ or Hˢᵉ) and a 'Next Encoder' (blue for text, red for speech) for the current turn. Cross-attention mechanisms are used to compute interaction enhancements, with outputs denoted as F¹⁻ⁱⁿᵗʳᵃ, F¹⁻ⁱⁿᵗᵉʳ, etc. The HT-NT and HS-NS modules process same-modality interactions, while HT-NS and HS-NT handle cross-modality interactions. All modules use multi-head cross-attention layers, visualized as stacked blocks with arrows indicating information flow.

Arrows indicate data flow: black arrows represent general training and inference processes; orange arrows denote training-specific paths. Speaker embeddings are marked with red dots. The entire system is designed to leverage both intra- and inter-modal historical context for improved speech synthesis in conversational scenarios.
